agent.name: Flag
agent.strategy: Bull flag: pole, quiet drift, breakout
agent.description: Well-formed bull flags across the universe: forming flags with their trigger and stop, and breakouts on volume with the trade attached.

context.label: Well-formed
context.value: flag vol <= 70% of pole, pullback <= 40%, 5-8 sessions

setup.title: Flag
setup.label: 26% pole · 5-session flag · 28% pullback on 44% of pole volume

opportunities.reasoning: This flag is structurally messy: the retracement to $330.84 is only 28% of the pole, which is unusually shallow for a bull flag and suggests weak selling pressure rather than healthy consolidation. The trigger at $337.28 (barely above today's close) offers poor risk/reward with the stop right at the flag bottom—a break below $330.84 would likely cascade given the shallow setup, while a breakout would need a decisive close above $350+ to prove the pattern, not just a squeeze through $337. Until the flag either decisively breaks $350.47 or collapses below $330, this looks more like a stock grinding sideways after a sharp run than a coiled spring.

setup.title: Flag
setup.label: 20% pole · 8-session flag · 31% pullback on 43% of pole volume

opportunities.reasoning:
# IDT Flag Assessment

This is a **stock losing momentum disguised as a flag**—the 31% retracement is shallow (flags typically hold 33-50%), and critically, the flag is forming on only 42% of pole volume, suggesting weak conviction in both directions. Confirmation would require a decisive break above $82.32 on volume expansion matching or exceeding the pole; breakdown below $80.22 is more likely given the anemic consolidation and that forming flags have shown poor historical edge.

setup.title: Flag
setup.label: 35% pole · 6-session flag · 39% pullback on 49% of pole volume

opportunities.reasoning:
# PATK Flag Assessment

This is a **weakly-formed flag with downside bias**: the flag retraced 39% of the pole (healthy compression) but the low volume on the flag itself suggests weak accumulation rather than institutional support, and the trigger at $80.65 sits just 0.05% below today's close—offering almost no margin of safety. Confirmation requires a clean break above $86.48 on expanding volume; breakdown below $77.75 kills it, but statistically incomplete flags like this one break down more often than they break out, especially after a 2.7% pump into resistance.

setup.title: Flag
setup.label: 30% pole · 5-session flag · 30% pullback on 57% of pole volume

opportunities.reasoning: This flag is structurally clean but contextually weak: the pullback consumed 57% of pole volume (healthy compression), yet it retraced 83% of the 30% move ($183.33 to $197.00), leaving minimal room for upside relative to the risk. Confirmation requires a break above $188.28 on volume expansion matching or exceeding the pole's setup volume; conversely, dropping below $183.33 kills it entirely. The real tell: most flags that hold this much of their pole's gains in the pullback fail to extend, so you'd need to see accelerating volume on the breakout to distinguish this from simple mean reversion.
